q: can I give Motrin to my 8 month old for fever
text: No — ibuprofen (Motrin) is not for babies under 6 months, and at 8 months it can be used, but only if your child is not dehydrated, does not have chickenpox, and does not have asthma unless a doctor has said it is OK [2]. Acetaminophen (Tylenol) and ibuprofen both reduce fever in children; give ibuprofen every 6 to 8 hours, and know your child's weight before giving it [6]. The dose depends on the child's weight — check the packaging or leaflet to make sure the medicine is suitable, or ask a pharmacist or doctor if you are not sure [3]. Keep breastfeeding or offering plenty of fluids, and watch for signs of dehydration [3]. Get medical advice if you are worried, or if the medicine is not helping [3].

q: my son threw up twice this morning, what should I give him to drink
text:
For vomiting, the main thing is to keep fluids going in, in small amounts often. Give your son small sips of an oral rehydration solution to replace the fluids and electrolytes he has lost — you can buy these without a prescription [1][6]. Offer them regularly rather than a large amount at once, and carry on with his usual diet in small amounts [6].

Avoid fruit juice and fizzy drinks, which can make vomiting worse [6]. If he is on formula or solid foods, small sips of extra water are fine too [6].

Get help if he shows signs of dehydration, or if vomiting continues — a health professional should be consulted for persistent symptoms or signs of dehydration [3].

q: how do I know if my child is getting dehydrated from vomiting
text:
Vomiting is one of the causes of dehydration, which happens when the body loses more fluid than it takes in [1]. The main risk of vomiting is dehydration, according to the SEUP [3].

To prevent it, give oral rehydration solution: when your child vomits, wait 20 minutes, then give 2–5 ml every 5 minutes for an hour [5]. If they keep it down, you can slowly increase how often you give it [5]. Don't use homemade solutions or fizzy drinks [5]. Oral rehydration fluids from the pharmacy are the most helpful for mild dehydration, and sports drinks without caffeine can also help, according to the CDC [2].

See your doctor if your child is very drowsy, vomits many times, or won't take fluids [3]. If you think they are severely dehydrated, call your doctor [2].

A cough that is worse at night is common in children with asthma, and it can also be the first sign of a cold-like illness such as croup or whooping cough [4][5][3]. Asthma symptoms usually come and go and are often worse at night and early in the morning, according to the NHS [4].

q: my son has been coughing for a week after a cold
text:
A cough that lingers after a cold is common, and cold symptoms can last 10 to 14 days [6]. If the cough is coming in bouts that are worse at night, or your son makes a "whoop" sound gasping between coughs, that points to whooping cough rather than a simple cold [4].

Keep him comfortable and offer fluids often. Coughs after a cold usually settle on their own as the cold runs its course [6].

Whooping cough starts like a cold, then after about a week brings coughing bouts lasting minutes, worse at night, sometimes with a whoop or vomiting after coughing, and the cough can last several weeks or months [4]. In babies under 3 months it can be different and more serious [4].

If you think it could be whooping cough, or he is getting worse rather than better, ask your doctor to see him [3].

q: he has a cough but no fever and is eating normally
text:
A cough without a fever, with normal eating, is usually nothing to worry about. A high temperature is the body's natural response to fighting infections like coughs and colds, according to the NHS [1].

Keep offering fluids and let him rest. If a fever does appear, the AEPap says you can give paracetamol every 4 to 6 hours, no more than five doses a day, or ibuprofen every 6 to 8 hours — the dose depends on the child's weight [6]. Do not alternate the two unless a doctor tells you to [1].

See your doctor if he stops wanting to eat, is not his usual self, or seems dehydrated, such as nappies that are not very wet or no tears when crying [1].

q: my 6 year old fell from the bed and hit the back of his head
text:
Most head injuries in children are not serious, but any symptom needs medical help [2]. After a knock like this, the usual symptoms are headache, confusion, brief memory loss, dizziness, nausea, vomiting and drowsiness [1].

For the headache you can give ibuprofen or paracetamol in the dose your doctor indicates [6]. Let him rest physically and mentally for 24 to 48 hours, with no sport and no screens, then return to normal activities gradually [4]. He can eat normally, and he can sleep — for a more significant knock, it is worth waking him every 4 hours [6].

Go to the emergency department if he has any of the symptoms above, or a behaviour that worries you; also if the fall was from more than one metre [5]. The NHS lists signs needing urgent help: being knocked out, not staying awake, a seizure, vision or hearing problems, clear fluid or blood from the ears or nose, bruising behind the ears, new numbness or weakness, trouble walking or speaking, or a change in behaviour [2].

q: what foods should I start with for a baby who just turned 6 months
text:
Start with single vegetables and fruits: mashed or soft, cooked sticks of parsnip, broccoli, potato, yam, sweet potato, carrot, apple or pear, according to the NHS [1]. Include less sweet vegetables like broccoli, cauliflower and spinach so your baby gets used to a range of flavours [1]. Let any cooked food cool right down before offering it [1].

At first, how much they eat matters less than getting used to eating — they still get most of their energy and nutrients from breast milk or first infant formula [2]. Introduce foods containing allergens, such as peanuts, hens' eggs, gluten and fish, from around 6 months, one at a time and in small amounts so you can spot any reaction [1]. Full-fat dairy like pasteurised cheese and plain yoghurt can be given from around 6 months; cows' milk only in cooking or mixed with food, not as a main drink until 1 year [1]. Babies do not need salt or sugar added to their food or cooking water [1].

q: how much water can a 9 month old drink
text:
For a 9-month-old, breast milk or formula is what meets all their nutritional needs [5]. The sources do not give a set amount of plain water for this age.

If your baby is losing fluids from vomiting or diarrhoea, the guidance is to give an oral rehydration solution (ORS) by mouth in frequent small sips, and to keep breastfeeding [1]. Plain water alone is not what the sources recommend for replacing those losses.

If your baby cannot drink, is drinking poorly, or is not improving with fluids, they need to be seen urgently [1].

q: my daughter is 13 months and still mostly drinks formula
text:
Once your child is 12 months old, formula milks are not needed — that includes first infant formula, follow-on formula, growing-up milks and toddler milks [1]. She can now drink pasteurised whole cows' milk as her main drink [1][3]. The AAP says that after 1 year, a child should only get whole milk, not skim or reduced-fat milk [4].

At 13 months she should be eating 3 meals a day with a variety of foods — starchy foods like potatoes, bread and rice; fruit and vegetables; milk or dairy products; and protein from meat, fish, eggs, dhal, beans, chickpeas or lentils — plus 2 healthy snacks in between meals [1]. Choose full-fat dairy such as cheese, yoghurt and fromage frais, because children under 2 need the vitamins and extra energy in them [1]. Offer snacks like soft fruit pieces, cooked or raw vegetable sticks, plain unsweetened full-fat yoghurt, cheese sticks, toast fingers, or unsweetened rice or corn cakes [1]. Do not give rice drinks under 5 years old because of the arsenic levels [1].

q: how often should a newborn poop
text: How often a newborn poops varies from baby to baby — the rhythm and consistency of stools differ from one person to another, and it is not essential that a baby has a bowel movement every day, according to the SEUP [3]. What matters more is the consistency: constipation is when stools become too hard, with discomfort or incomplete emptying, and it may come with fewer bowel movements [6]. In a baby under 6 months, keep feeding as usual with breast milk or formula [3]. Do not give laxatives or enemas without asking your doctor [3]. See your doctor if there is blood in the stool, a lot of tummy pain, or the baby vomits many times and cannot keep down solids or liquids [3].

q: my 4 year old wakes up coughing only when he lies down
text:
A cough that comes on mainly when he lies down can be a sign of asthma, which often makes coughing worse at night [3]. Asthma is a long-term condition where the airways become inflamed and narrowed, causing coughing, wheezing and chest tightness [4]. Symptoms usually come and go and are often worse at night and early in the morning [5].

Keep the room air moist — a steamy shower or a vaporizer can help ease a cough [1]. Do not give cough medicine to a child under four; for children over four, use caution and read labels carefully [1].

See your doctor if your child has asthma symptoms, or if symptoms are waking him up at night [5]. Get medical help right away if there is severe coughing, serious breathing problems, or the face, lips or fingernails turn very pale or blue [3].

On steam, guidelines differ. The CDC suggests sitting with a young child in a bathroom with steam from a running shower to ease a cough. The NHS advises against it: with croup, do not put your child in a steamy room or get them to inhale steam, and do not let children breathe in steam from a bowl of hot water, because of the risk of scalding.

q: my son has asthma and is using albuterol more than usual
text: Asthma cannot be cured, but the right treatment lets most people live a normal, active life, according to the WHO [1]. Using a reliever inhaler such as salbutamol more often than usual is a sign the treatment is not working well enough, and the NHS says to see your doctor if your child is needing to use their inhaler more often or needs advice about using it [2]. Make sure the inhaler is used correctly, with a spacer if you have one, since that helps the medicine reach the lungs [1]. A doctor, nurse or pharmacist can show you how to use it properly [3]. If your child is having an attack — severe breathing problems, struggling to breathe — sit them up straight, stay calm, and give 1 puff of the reliever inhaler every 30 to 60 seconds, up to 10 puffs, shaking it between puffs [4]. Get emergency help if they feel worse at any time or do not feel better after the maximum dose [4].

q: she is making a strange noise when she breathes but is still smiling
text:
A strange noise when breathing can be croup: an inflammation of the vocal cords and windpipe that causes noisy, sharp sounds on breathing in, often with a barking cough and a hoarse voice, according to MedlinePlus [3]. It often starts like a cold, the symptoms usually get worse at night and last three to five days, and most viral cases are mild and can be treated at home [3].

Keep her calm and comfortable, and let her rest; sitting her up can help her breathe more easily [3].

If you are worried about her breathing, call your doctor straight away [3]. Signs that breathing is getting harder are breathing fast, the ribs pulling in, the chest dipping in, or tiring when walking or running, according to the SEUP [1].

q: my baby had a seizure last year and has a fever today
text:
A febrile seizure can happen when a child has a high temperature, and it is not usually serious, according to the NHS [3]. They usually affect children between 6 months and 6 years old and last 2 to 3 minutes [2].

If your child has a fever today, you can check their temperature with a digital thermometer under the arm; a high temperature is 38C (100.4 °F) or more [1]. The temperature usually returns to normal within 1 to 4 days [1]. You cannot prevent febrile seizures [6].

Get medical help if your child has a seizure [3]. Call your local emergency number or go to the emergency department if a seizure lasts more than 5 minutes, if they have difficulty breathing, twitching on only one side, are more sleepy than usual for over an hour afterwards, or have more than one seizure within 24 hours [2]. Do not put anything in your child's mouth or try to hold them still during a seizure [5].

q: my 4 year old had a seizure when he was a baby, does that change anything now
text:
A febrile seizure can seem frightening, but it is unlikely to harm your child or cause long-term effects, according to the NHS [2]. Children who have had one have a slightly increased chance of epilepsy later in life, but this is rare [3].

If your child ever has another seizure, keep them safe while you wait for medical help: check the time it starts and ends, protect their head with your hands or something soft, and remove any dangerous objects nearby [4]. q: my son is 4 and weighs 25 pounds, is that too little

What to do now: your paediatrician can judge this properly by plotting his weight and height on the growth curves over time, rather than from a single weight. q: my son had croup last winter and now has a barking cough again
text:
A barking cough that comes on suddenly at night, after a few days of cold-like symptoms, is the usual pattern of croup, according to the SEUP [3]. Croup is an inflammation of the vocal cords and windpipe, usually caused by a virus, and most cases are mild and can be treated at home [1].

Offer fluids if there is a fever and give the usual fever medicine [4]. Water can help ease the cough, whether your son drinks it or you add it to the air with a steamy shower or vaporizer [6]. Do not give cough medicine to a child under four [6].

Croup symptoms are often worse at night and usually last about three to five days, though they can persist up to a week [1][4]. Watch his breathing and his colour and general condition, because in some cases the swelling makes it harder for air to get in [4]. If you are worried about his breathing, call your doctor right away [1].

On steam, guidelines differ. The CDC suggests sitting with a young child in a bathroom with steam from a running shower to ease a cough. The NHS advises against it: with croup, do not put your child in a steamy room or get them to inhale steam, and do not let children breathe in steam from a bowl of hot water, because of the risk of scalding.

q: what should I know about malaria symptoms in a child returning from Africa
text:
The most common early symptoms of malaria are fever, headache and chills, and they usually start within 10–15 days of being bitten by an infected mosquito, according to the WHO [4]. Early symptoms can be mild and look like many other illnesses, so getting tested early matters [4]. Children under 5 are at higher risk of severe infection [4].

Severe symptoms to know about include extreme tiredness, impaired consciousness, multiple convulsions, difficulty breathing, dark or bloody urine, jaundice and abnormal bleeding; someone with these needs emergency care right away [4]. Getting treatment early for mild malaria can stop it becoming severe [4].

If you travelled to a malaria area, tell your doctor about the trip so they can test for it [4].

q: my daughter fainted for a few seconds at school and feels fine now
text:
A short faint like this is called a syncope: a sudden, brief loss of consciousness that happens when not enough blood or oxygen reaches the brain, according to the SEUP [2]. It is often triggered by heat, pain, fear, nerves, standing still for a long time, or getting up suddenly [2]. Children usually recover quickly after a short rest, within a couple of minutes [5].

If she starts to feel unwell again, have her sit or lie down right away, breathe slowly and deeply, and get up slowly afterwards [5]. It also helps children who tend to faint to drink more fluids, especially with exercise [4].

Get urgent help if she takes more than 3 to 5 minutes to come round, if the faint happened during exercise or while sitting, or if it came with palpitations, chest pain, jerking of the limbs or passing urine [6].

q: my toddler has very hard poop and cries when he goes
text:
Hard, dry poop that hurts to pass is constipation, and in most cases it lasts a short time and is not serious [3]. Constipation means fewer than three bowel movements a week, with stool that can be hard and dry and sometimes painful to pass [3].

What helps: offer more liquids, preferably water, to soften the stool and make it easier to pass, and more meals with fiber — wholegrain cereals and bread, fruit and vegetables. Don't replace fruit with juice, since juice has little fiber [1]. More fruit, vegetables and grains, plenty of water and other liquids, and enough exercise all help prevent it [3]. Don't give laxatives or enemas without checking with your doctor [1].

See your doctor if there is blood in the stool, bad abdominal pain, or if he is very down and complaining a lot, or vomiting repeatedly and keeping nothing down [1].

Heat exhaustion can follow being out in the heat too long, and it can turn into heatstroke, which is a life-threatening illness [3]. Itchy red patches on the arms are common in children and often fit with eczema, a skin condition that makes skin dry and itchy [1]. Scratching can make the skin redder, more swollen and itchier, so try to stop the scratching [2].

text: It's natural to worry when a child refuses to eat sometimes, and it's perfectly normal for young children to refuse to eat or even taste new foods [3]. Don't worry about what your child eats in a day or if they don't finish a meal — it's more helpful to think about what they eat over a week [3]. If your child is active, gaining weight and seems well, they're getting enough to eat [3]. Keep offering a variety of foods and go back to foods they refused before; tastes change, and it may take many attempts before they accept something [3]. Give small portions, praise them even if they only eat a little, and don't force them — just take the food away without saying anything and try again another time [2]. A stomach ache can also be a sign of constipation, so it's worth checking how often they've been passing poo [6].

text: No wet nappy for 3 hours or more is a sign of dehydration in infants, according to MedlinePlus [2]. Keep offering fluids: during illness, increase fluid intake, including more frequent breastfeeding, and offer soft, favourite foods [3]. Oral rehydration solutions that come already prepared are the best way to replace losses — do not use homemade solutions or commercial soft drinks [1]. Do not give medicines for diarrhoea or vomiting without checking with your paediatrician [1]. Get medical help right away if there is confusion, fainting, lack of urination, rapid heartbeat or rapid breathing [2].

q: my baby is 4 months and has a fever of 38
text: A fever is usually the body's normal response to fighting an infection, and it should come down over 1 to 4 days [1]. Keep breastfeeding as normal, offer plenty of fluids, and check on your baby regularly, including during the night [1]. Keep them at home and don't undress them or sponge them down to cool them [1][7]. If your baby is distressed or uncomfortable, the NHS says you can give either paracetamol or ibuprofen, checking the packaging or leaflet to make sure the medicine is suitable for your child, or speaking to a pharmacist or doctor if you're not sure [1]. Because your baby is 4 months old, ibuprofen should not be given without a doctor's advice [7]. Get medical advice if you're worried about your child, or if the medicine is not helping [1].

q: my child got fever after vaccination yesterday
text:
If your child is under 3 months old, a fever needs a doctor the same day.

For an older child, a fever in the day or two after a vaccination is common and usually settles on its own. The rotavirus vaccine, for example, is a live, weakened virus given by mouth from 6 weeks of age [2]. Keep offering fluids often and dress them lightly; you do not need to give a fever medicine, and if you do, the dose depends on your child's age and weight, so follow your doctor's or the leaflet's instructions.

Vaccines are given at well-child visits, following the recommended schedule, so protection builds before exposure to serious diseases [3]. In India the ages and doses follow India's national immunisation schedule, which may differ from the schedules published elsewhere [3].

If the fever is high, lasts more than a few days, or your child is drowsy, feeding poorly or breathing fast, see your doctor.

q: my son fell from bed and vomited twice
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Vomiting after a head injury
text:
First, do what the warning above says.

A child who vomits after a head injury needs to be checked, and the SEUP says repeated vomiting is one of the signs to watch for after a knock to the head [1]. Keep them resting, both physically and mentally, for 24 to 48 hours, with no sport and no screens, and return to normal activities gradually [1]. While you are on the way, watch for a severe or worsening headache that does not ease with paracetamol or ibuprofen, more vomiting, confusion or drowsiness, irritability or difficulty waking, changes in behaviour, trouble speaking or walking, or blood or clear fluid from the nose or ears [1].

q: my daughter has mosquito bites all over her legs, what can I put
text: Mosquito bites usually just itch, and they should get better in a few days [5][1]. Put an ice pack wrapped in a cloth, or a clean cloth soaked in cold water, on the bites for at least 20 minutes, and keep the area raised if it's swollen, according to the NHS [1]. You can give painkillers such as paracetamol or ibuprofen if they're painful, and use antihistamines to relieve the itching [1]. A hydrocortisone cream can also reduce itching and swelling [1]. Don't let her scratch the bites, as they could get infected, and don't use home remedies like bicarbonate of soda [7]. See a pharmacist if the skin around a bite feels hot, looks red, is painful or swollen, or has pus or fluid coming out [7].

q: my 3 year old is coughing mostly at night, should I use a nebulizer
text: A night-time cough in a 3-year-old is common with several illnesses, and none of the guidance here describes using a nebulizer for it. A cough that is worse at night can be part of whooping cough, whose coughing fits get worse and happen more often at night, according to MedlinePlus [1]. Croup also causes a barking cough that is often worse at night, according to the NHS [5]. Asthma symptoms such as coughing and wheezing may be worse at night and early in the morning, and the NHS advises seeing a doctor if your child has asthma symptoms, or if symptoms are waking them at night [4]. RSV causes cold-like symptoms including coughing and wheezing, according to the Government of Canada [2]. If you think your child may have croup, ask for an urgent appointment — the doctor may give medicine to shorten the illness [5].

q: my son has been vomiting since morning and cannot keep ORS down
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Vomits everything and keeps nothing down: it is a danger sign — get seen today
text:
Vomiting that keeps everything down is a danger sign, and the main risk from vomiting is dehydration [1][6].

Keep offering oral rehydration solution in small, frequent sips rather than a large amount at once, and continue breastfeeding or formula as usual — small amounts more often than usual [7]. Do not water down formula, and avoid fruit juice or fizzy drinks, which can make vomiting worse [7]. If your child is drowsy, vomiting many times, or not taking fluids, contact your paediatrician [6].

Get seen today if your child is under 3 months and has vomited two or more feeds, is vomiting green, bloody or coffee-ground material, is drowsy or floppy, very thirsty, has sunken eyes, cries without tears or is passing little urine, or has severe tummy pain or headache [4].

q: मेरे बच्चे को कल से दस्त हो रहे हैं और वह खाना नहीं खा रहा
text:
दस्त में ओरल रीहाइड्रेशन सॉल्ट (ORS) और ज़िंक सप्लीमेंट दोनों ज़रूरी इलाज हैं, ऐसा विश्व स्वास्थ्य संगठन कहता है [1][3]। ORS साफ पानी, नमक और चीनी का घोल है, जो दस्त में खोए पानी और नमक की भरपाई करता है [1]। ज़िंक दस्त की अवधि लगभग 25% तक घटाता है और मल की मात्रा भी कम करता है [1]। ज़िंक की खुराक और कितने दिन देनी है, यह डॉक्टर या दवा के पर्चे के अनुसार तय होगी [3]।

खाना खाने की इच्छा न होने पर भी पोषक आहार देना बंद न करें — दस्त के दौरान भी पौष्टिक भोजन और माँ का दूध जारी रखें, इससे कुपोषण और दस्त का चक्र टूटता है [1]। बच्चे को साफ कटोरी और चम्मच से खिलाएँ, बोतल से नहीं [2]।

अगर दस्त लंबे समय तक बने रहें, मल में खून आए, या पानी की कमी के लक्षण दिखें, तो स्वास्थ्य कर्मी से सलाह लें [1]।

q: मेरे बच्चे को बुखार के साथ लाल दाने निकल आए हैं
text:
अगर बच्चा 3 महीने से छोटा है, तो बुखार में उसी दिन डॉक्टर को दिखाना ज़रूरी है।

बुखार के साथ लाल दाने कई चीज़ों से हो सकते हैं। खसरा आमतौर पर ज़ुकाम जैसे लक्षणों से शुरू होता है और कुछ दिन बाद दाने निकलते हैं; दाने चेहरे के बालों की लाइन से शुरू होकर नीचे गर्दन, धड़, बाज़ुओं, टाँगों और पैरों तक फैलते हैं, और दाने निकलते समय बुखार तेज़ हो सकता है [4]। चेचक में खुजली वाले दाने शरीर पर कहीं भी हो सकते हैं, और दाने से पहले या बाद में तेज़ बुखार, बदन दर्द और भूख न लगना भी हो सकता है [5]। हैंड, फुट एंड माउथ डिज़ीज़ में पहले गले में दर्द और तेज़ बुखार होता है, फिर मुँह में छाले और हाथ-पैरों पर उभरे दाने निकलते हैं [3]।

दाने दिखने पर डॉक्टर को दिखाएँ, ताकि पता चले कि कारण क्या है [1]।

बच्चे की उम्र कितनी है? उम्र जानकर मैं जवाब और सटीक कर सकता हूँ।

q: मेरा 6 महीने का बच्चा दूध कम पी रहा है और पेशाब भी कम कर रहा है
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: पानी की कमी के लक्षण: आँखें धँसी, कम पेशाब, सूखा मुँह, लगातार उल्टी या 24 घंटे से ज़्यादा दस्त
text:
6 महीने के बच्चे में दूध कम पीना और पेशाब कम होना निर्जलीकरण का संकेत हो सकता है, और जितना छोटा बच्चा हो, निर्जलीकरण का खतरा उतना ही ज़्यादा होता है [1]।

अभी ओरल रीहाइड्रेशन सॉल्यूशन (ORS) थोड़ी-थोड़ी मात्रा में, बार-बार देना शुरू करें — घर के बने घोल या कोल्ड ड्रिंक इसके लिए नहीं इस्तेमाल करें [1]। स्तनपान सामान्य रूप से, और अगर बच्चा माँगे तो उससे भी ज़्यादा बार जारी रखें; दूध छुड़ाने की ज़रूरत नहीं है [8]। दस्त या उल्टी की दवा बिना डॉक्टर से पूछे न दें [1]।

अगर बच्चा बहुत प्यासा लगे, बिना आँसू के रोए, पेशाब कम करे या आँखें धँसी दिखें, या चिड़चिड़ापन, सुस्ती या जवाब देने में कमी हो, तो तुरंत डॉक्टर के पास ले जाएँ [1]।

q: मेरी बेटी बिस्तर से गिर गई और उसके बाद एक बार उल्टी हुई
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: सिर पर चोट के बाद उल्टी
text:
सिर की चोट के बाद उल्टी होना ऐसा लक्षण है जिस पर डॉक्टर तुरंत ध्यान देते हैं, इसलिए बेटी को आज ही दिखाना ज़रूरी है [1]। रास्ते में उसे आराम से लिटाकर रखें, हिलाने-डुलाने से बचें, और कुछ भी खाने-पीने को ज़बरदस्ती न दें [1]।

SEUP के मुताबिक चोट के बाद 24 से 48 घंटे शारीरिक और मानसिक आराम ज़रूरी है — खेल-कूद और मोबाइल, टैबलेट, वीडियो गेम जैसी चीज़ें बंद रखें, और बाद में धीरे-धीरे सामान्य दिनचर्या पर लौटें [1]।

अगर सिर में तेज़ या बढ़ता दर्द हो जो आम दर्द की दवा से भी ठीक न हो, बार-बार उल्टी हो, वह भ्रमित या बेसुध जैसी लगे, बहुत चिड़चिड़ी हो या जगाना मुश्किल हो, चलने-बोलने में दिक्कत हो, या नाक या कान से खून या साफ़ तरल निकले — तो यह गंभीर होने का संकेत है [1]।

q: बच्चे को कब्ज है और पॉटी करते समय बहुत रोता है
text:
कब्ज़ शिशुओं में रोने का एक आम कारण है, और मल त्याग के समय तकलीफ़ होने पर बच्चा रो सकता है [2]। कब्ज़ कोलिक जैसी स्थितियों से जुड़ी एक वजह भी मानी जाती है [5]।

अभी के लिए, बच्चे को आराम पहुँचाने की कोशिश करें और रोना शांत होने का इंतज़ार करें — कभी-कभी इसके अलावा ज़्यादा कुछ नहीं किया जा सकता [1]। अगर पता न चले कि क्या परेशानी है, तो अपने डॉक्टर से बात करना सबसे अच्छा है [2]।

अगर रोना लगातार हो और बच्चा शांत ही न हो, या रोना उसके सामान्य रोने जैसा न लगे, तो यह बीमारी का संकेत हो सकता है — ऐसे में डॉक्टर से संपर्क करें [4]।

q: मेरे बच्चे के हाथ पैर ठंडे हैं लेकिन शरीर गर्म है
text:
बुखार चढ़ते समय बच्चे का ठंड लगना और हाथ-पैर ठंडे होना सामान्य है — त्वचा पर जाल जैसा रंग भी दिख सकता है, खासकर हाथों और पैरों पर। जब बुखार उतरता है तो बच्चा पसीना-पसीना और गर्म हो जाता है, यह SEUP के अनुसार होता है [1]।

बुखार आमतौर पर 2 से 4 दिन रहता है, और दवा देने के बाद भी पूरी तरह न उतरे तो यह सामान्य बात है [2]। बुखार शरीर की रक्षा का तरीका है, अपने आप में गंभीरता की निशानी नहीं [5]। बच्चे को पर्याप्त तरल देना ज़रूरी है ताकि पानी की कमी न हो [4]।

घर पर बच्चे की सामान्य हालत और रंग पर ध्यान रखें, और अगर त्वचा पर लाल चकत्ते दिखें जो दबाने पर भी न मिटें, तो डॉक्टर से मिलें [2]।

q: मेरा बच्चा बहुत सुस्त है और ठीक से जाग नहीं रहा

text:

रास्ते में बच्चे को माँ की गोद में या खटिया पर लिटाकर रखें और साँसों की गति देखते रहें [3]। छह महीने से कम उम्र के शिशु में 60 से अधिक, छह महीने से दो साल के बच्चे में 50 से अधिक और दो साल से ऊपर के बच्चे में 40 से अधिक साँस प्रति मिनट तेज श्वसन माना जाता है [3]। बच्चे का खाना-पीना चालू रखने की कोशिश करें [2]।

अगर साँस लेते समय पसलियाँ अंदर खिंचती दिखें, सीने से कराहने या सीटी जैसी आवाज आए, या त्वचा, होंठ, नाखून व चेहरे पर नीली झलक दिखे, तो यह और गंभीरता का संकेत है [2]।

q: मेरे बच्चे ने आज बहुत कम पेशाब किया है
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: पानी की कमी के लक्षण: आँखें धँसी, कम पेशाब, सूखा मुँह, लगातार उल्टी या 24 घंटे से ज़्यादा दस्त
text:
बहुत कम पेशाब आना निर्जलीकरण का संकेत हो सकता है — SEUP के अनुसार अगर बच्चा बहुत प्यासा लगे, बिना आँसू के रोए, कम पेशाब करे या आँखें धँसी लगें, तो यह चिंता की बात है [1]।

अब सबसे ज़रूरी है निर्जलीकरण रोकना। बच्चे को ओरल रिहाइड्रेशन सॉल्यूशन (ORS) थोड़ी-थोड़ी मात्रा में, बार-बार दें — घर के बने घोल या कोल्ड ड्रिंक्स इसके लिए नहीं इस्तेमाल करने चाहिए [1]। दस्त या उल्टी की दवा बिना बाल रोग विशेषज्ञ से पूछे न दें [1]।

खाना बंद करने की ज़रूरत नहीं; बच्चा सामान्य खाना खा सकता है, बस थोड़ी-थोड़ी मात्रा में और ज़्यादा बार दें। चिकनी चीज़ें, मिठाई और जूस से बचें; दूध और स्तनपान जारी रखें। स्पोर्ट्स ड्रिंक्स न दें [8]।

अगर बच्चा बहुत उल्टी करे, कुछ भी न रुके, या उल्टी हरी, खून वाली या कॉफ़ी जैसी भूरी हो, तो तुरंत आपातकालीन विभाग जाएँ [8]।

बड़े बच्चे में तेज बुखार के साथ बैंगनी दाग — यानी ऐसे दाने जो दबाने पर भी नहीं मिटते — एक चेतावनी संकेत हैं, और ऐसे में तुरंत इलाज की ज़रूरत होती है [1][2]। NHS के मुताबिक ऐसे दानों के साथ बुखार होने पर बच्चे को तुरंत अस्पताल ले जाना चाहिए [2]।

जाते समय: बच्चे को ज़्यादा कपड़ों या रज़ाई में न लपेटें, और उसे ठंडा करने के लिए कपड़े उतारकर स्पंज न करें — बुखार शरीर की स्वाभाविक प्रतिक्रिया है [2]। 16 साल से कम उम्र के बच्चे को एस्पिरिन न दें [2]। बुखार नापने के लिए डिजिटल थर्मामीटर बगल में रखें [3]।

q: mere 3 saal ke bacche ko bukhar 102 hai, paracetamol kitna du
text:
Aapke 3 saal ke bacche ko bukhar hai, to paracetamol dene se pehle bacche ka wazan pata hona chahiye, kyunki iski dose wazan ke hisaab se tay hoti hai [3]. Aap PediBot ke dose calculator se sahi matra nikaal sakte hain.

Paracetamol har 4 se 6 ghante mein diya ja sakta hai, aur din mein paanch se zyada baar nahi [3]. Ibuprofen har 6 se 8 ghante mein diya ja sakta hai, lekin agar lagatar ulti ho rahi ho to ise na dein [3]. AEPap ke mutabik, shuruaat paracetamol se karein [3].

Agar 3-4 ghante baad bhi bukhar tez hai aur bacche ko aaram nahi mil raha, to agle antitypik ko badalna theek hai [3]. Dawa shuru karne se pehle apne bachche ke doctor ki salah lein [5].

q: mera baby raat ko bahut khans raha hai
text:
Raat ko khansi bachchon mein asthma ka ek aam lakshan hai — MedlinePlus ke mutabik khansi khaas taur par raat mein ya subah jaldi hoti hai [1]. SEUP bhi kehta hai ki bachchon mein khansi, saans ki takleef aur seeti jaisi awaaz (sibilancias) ho sakti hai, aur kabhi yeh symptoms zukam ke baad shuru hote hain [4].

Agar saans phool rahi ho, seeti ki awaaz aaye ya seene mein jakadan ho, to doctor se milna zaroori hai [1][4]. Agar khansi teen hafte ya usse zyada rahe, to bhi jaanch karani chahiye [2].

Dhyan dein: tez khansi, saans lene mein badi dikkat, ya chehre, hothon aur naakhunon ka rang neela padna gambhir attack ke warning signs hain — aise mein turant medical help lein [1].

q: mere bete ke pairon par lal dane hain aur khujli ho rahi hai
text:
Aapke bete ke pairon par lal dane aur khujli heat rash (prickly heat) ke lakshan ho sakte hain: chhote, ubhre hue dane, khujli ya chubhan wali feeling aur halki sujan, jo NHS ke mutabik heat rash ke symptoms hain [6].

Abhi sabse zaroori hai skin ko thanda rakhna taaki pasina aakar rash ko aur na chidhaye [6]. Dheele cotton kapde pehnaiye, halki bedding use kijiye, thande paani se nahiye ya nahlaiye, aur dehydration se bachne ke liye khoob paani pilaiye [6]. Khujli ya chubhan kam karne ke liye thandi cheez jaise geele kapde ya ice pack (towel mein lipti hui) ko 20 minute tak lagaiye, aur rash ko khurachne ke bajaye thap-thap kijiye [6]. Perfumed shower gel ya cream mat lagaiye [6].

Agar aapko yakeen nahi hai ki ye heat rash hai, to doosre rashes ke baare mein dekhiye [6].

q: mere bacche ko kabz hai aur potty karte waqt rota hai
text:
Kabz ke karan bacche ka potty karte waqt rona ho sakta hai: NHS ke mutabik constipation un karanon mein se ek hai jinki wajah se bacche rote hain [3]. SEUP bhi kehta hai ki kabz un wajahon mein shamil hai jinke bare mein socha jata hai ki isse infant colic ho sakta hai [2].

Jo aap abhi kar sakte hain: apne bacche ko tasalli dene ki koshish karein aur rone ke thamne ka intezar karein [1]. Agar aapko samajh nahi aa raha ki kya galat hai, to apne doctor se baat karein ya apne local emergency number par call karein [3].

Turant madad lein agar bacche ko bukhar ho, doodh peene mein dilchaspi na ho, ya wo bechain ho aur aap use shant na kar paayein [7].

q: mere bete ko saans lene mein dikkat lag rahi hai

text:
सबसे पहले, ऊपर की चेतावनी में जो लिखा है वह कीजिए।

Saans lene mein dikkat kai cheezon se ho sakti hai, jaise bronchiolitis ya RSV, jo shuruaat mein sardi-jaisi halki lagti hai aur kuch dinon mein badh sakti hai [2][5]. Bronchiolitis mein shuruaati lakshan zukaam jaise hote hain — chheenkna, naak behna ya band hona, halka bukhar — phir khansi, tez saans aur wheezing aa sakti hai [5].

Abhi ke liye: bachche ko seedha aur aaram se rakhein, thoda-thoda doodh ya paani baar-baar dein taaki wo dehydrated na ho, aur naak saaf rakhein [5]. Agar wo doodh peena kam kar de ya nappy 12 ghante sookha rahe to ye dehydration ka sanket hai [5].

Agar bachcha bahut thak gaya ho, irritable ho, ya pehle se zyada beemar lag raha ho to turant doctor se milna zaroori hai [5].

text:
तेज़ साँस लेना शिशुओं में ब्रोंकियोलाइटिस या RSV जैसी साँस की बीमारी का संकेत हो सकता है — NHS के अनुसार ब्रोंकियोलाइटिस में बच्चा तेज़ी से साँस लेता है, साँस में घरघराहट होती है और दूध पीना कम कर देता है [3]। CDC के अनुसार RSV शुरू में हल्का लग सकता है, पर कुछ दिनों में गंभीर हो सकता है, और शुरुआती लक्षण नाक बहना, कम खाना-पीना और खाँसी हैं जो आगे चलकर घरघराहट या साँस लेने में कठिनाई बन सकते हैं [2]।

अभी बच्चे को गोद में सीधा और आराम से रखें, और थोड़ी-थोड़ी मात्रा में बार-बार दूध या तरल दें ताकि पानी की कमी न हो [3]। WHO के अनुसार पाँच साल से छोटे बच्चों में खाँसी या साँस लेने में कठिनाई के साथ तेज़ साँस चलना (टैकीप्निया) या पसलियों के नीचे धँसाव निमोनिया का संकेत है, और बहुत गंभीर हालत में बच्चा दूध पीना बंद कर सकता है [6]।

अगर बच्चा दूध पीना बंद कर दे, बेहोश या सुस्त हो जाए, या साँस में रुकावट दिखे तो तुरंत इलाज कराएँ [3][6]।

q: my 2 year old has bad cough at night not sleeping
text:
A cough that is worse at night is common in whooping cough (pertussis), an infection of the lungs and breathing tubes that spreads very easily and can be serious [3]. The first signs are like a cold — runny nose and sore throat — and after about a week come coughing bouts that last for a few minutes and are worse at night [3]. The cough may last for several weeks or months [3].

Keep the room cool and the bedding light, since sweating at night is normal when the room or bedding makes a child too hot [2]. Ask a pharmacist about cough medicine, but note that some cough medicines should not be given to children under 12 years old [1].

See a doctor if the cough has lasted more than 3 weeks, or if it is very bad or quickly gets worse, they feel very unwell, have chest pain, swollen and painful glands in the neck, difficulty breathing, or are coughing up blood [1].

q: my 5 year old baby has red pimples on full body
text:
A rash of small, raised bumps that feels rough, like sandpaper, could be scarlet fever, according to the NHS [5]. A spotty rash that starts on the head or neck and spreads to the rest of the body could be measles [5]. Measles usually starts with cold-like symptoms — a high temperature, runny or blocked nose, sneezing, cough, and red, sore, watery eyes — followed by a rash a few days later [5]. The measles rash begins as flat red spots at the hairline and spreads downward to the neck, trunk, arms, legs and feet, and small raised bumps may appear on top [4].

Speak to a GP if you think your child has scarlet fever or measles [5].

q: should I give polio drops if my baby already had injection
text: The polio vaccine is given as part of a combined vaccine, so your baby's schedule depends on which vaccines they have already had and when they were born [2]. The routine schedule gives the six-in-one vaccine (which includes polio) at eight, twelve and sixteen weeks old [2]. If your child missed a vaccination, contact your GP to catch up, and they will advise what vaccination your child should get and when [1][3]. It is important that vaccines are given on time for the best protection [3]. Speak to your child's health visitor or GP if you have any questions about the schedule [1].

q: my 6 year old child is not eating anything from 2 days
text: It's natural to worry when a child refuses to eat, but it's normal for children to refuse food sometimes [6]. Think about what they eat over a week rather than in a day, and if your child is active, gaining weight and seems well, they're getting enough to eat [6]. Keep offering a variety of foods from the 4 main food groups, give small portions, and praise them even if they only eat a little [6][3]. Eat with them when you can, since children learn to eat by copying you, and don't force or leave meals until they're too hungry or tired [3]. Keep snacks to about 2 healthy snacks a day between meals [3]. If your child is not active, is losing weight, or seems unwell, have them seen by your doctor [6].

text:
A whistling sound when a baby breathes can be wheezing, which is common in viral chest infections like bronchiolitis and RSV [2][4]. Symptoms are usually worst between days 3 and 5, and the cough usually gets better in about 3 weeks [2].

Keep feeding your baby little and often, since babies with these infections may feed less than usual [2][4]. Keep their nose clear if it is blocked, and keep them comfortable.

While you are on the way to be seen, keep your baby upright and calm, and watch their breathing [2]. If they cannot feed at all, have a dry nappy for 12 hours or more, or seem very tired or irritable, that needs urgent attention [2][4].

q: bukhar (उम्र: 6 महीने) (वज़न: 5 किलो)
text:
बुखार छोटे बच्चों में बहुत आम है और आमतौर पर 1 से 4 दिन में तापमान सामान्य हो जाता है [1]। 38°C या उससे ज़्यादा तापमान बुखार माना जाता है [1]।

अभी यह करें: बच्चे को खूब तरल दें — अगर स्तनपान कराती हैं तो सामान्य रूप से स्तनपान जारी रखें, निर्जलीकरण के संकेतों पर नज़र रखें, और अगर बच्चा खाना चाहे तो खाना दें [4]। रात में भी नियमित रूप से बच्चे को देखते रहें [4]। अगर बच्चा परेशान या असहज लगे तो पैरासिटामोल या आइबुप्रोफेन दें — पैकेजिंग या पत्ते पर देखें कि दवा आपके बच्चे के लिए उपयुक्त है या नहीं, या फार्मासिस्ट या डॉक्टर से पूछें [4]। 6 महीने के बच्चे को एस्पिरिन न दें [2]।

अगर बच्चा 3 से 6 महीने का है और तापमान 39°C या उससे ज़्यादा है, या बुखार के साथ दाने जैसे बीमारी के अन्य संकेत हैं, या बुखार 5 दिन या उससे ज़्यादा रहा है, या बच्चा खाना नहीं चाहता या सामान्य नहीं लग रहा और आप चिंतित हैं, या निर्जलीकरण के संकेत हैं — जैसे कम गीले नैपी, धँसी आँखें, रोते समय आँसू न आना — तो तुरंत चिकित्सा सहायता लें [2]।

ध्यान दें: WHO के विकास चार्ट के अनुसार 6 महीने के बच्चे के लिए 5 किग्रा बहुत कम वज़न है। अगर वज़न सही है तो जल्द ही डॉक्टर से बच्चे की बढ़त जँचवाएँ; अगर लिखने में गलती हुई है तो उसे ठीक करें, क्योंकि दवा की खुराक वज़न से तय होती है।

q: क्या बुखार उतारने के लिए बच्चे को नहला सकती हूँ? (उम्र: 6 महीने) (वज़न: 5 किलो)
text:
बुखार में बच्चे को नहलाना या स्पंज करके ठंडा करने की कोशिश न करें — तेज़ तापमान शरीर की संक्रमण से लड़ने की स्वाभाविक और स्वस्थ प्रतिक्रिया है, ऐसा NHS कहता है [7]। बच्चे को ज़्यादा कपड़ों या रज़ाई में न लपेटें [7]।

बुखार उतारने के लिए गुनगुने पानी में कपड़ा भिगोकर पूरा शरीर पोंछें, सिर्फ माथा नहीं, और बच्चे का खाना-पीना चालू रखें, ऐसा विकासपीडिया बताता है [3]। छह महीने के बच्चे को पैरासिटामोल दी जा सकती है, पर आइबुप्रोफेन उस बच्चे को न दें जिसका वज़न 5 किलो से कम हो [7]। दोनों दवाएँ बारी-बारी न दें, जब तक डॉक्टर या नर्स न कहें [7]। खुराक बच्चे के वज़न के अनुसार तय होती है [7]।

अगर बच्चा दूध या खाना न ले रहा हो, सुस्त हो या पसलियाँ साँस लेते समय अंदर खिंच रही हों, तो तुरंत डॉक्टर से मिलें [3][7]।

ध्यान दें: WHO के विकास चार्ट के अनुसार 6 महीने के बच्चे के लिए 5 किग्रा बहुत कम वज़न है। अगर वज़न सही है तो जल्द ही डॉक्टर से बच्चे की बढ़त जँचवाएँ; अगर लिखने में गलती हुई है तो उसे ठीक करें, क्योंकि दवा की खुराक वज़न से तय होती है।

q: 3 साल के बच्चे को सूखी खांसी और छाती से सीटी की आवाज आ रही है
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: साँस की दिक्कत: तेज़ साँस, सीटी जैसी आवाज़, पसलियाँ दिखना
text:
3 साल के बच्चे में सूखी खांसी और सांस लेते समय सीटी जैसी आवाज़ सांस की नली में रुकावट के कारण होती है, जिसे घरघराहट कहते हैं [2]। यह अक्सर सर्दी-जुकाम जैसे वायरल संक्रमण से शुरू होती है, और स्कूल जाने से पहले की उम्र के बच्चों में घरघराहट का सबसे आम कारण यही संक्रमण होता है [2]।

ऐसे में बच्चे को सीधा बैठाकर रखें और शांत रखें, और सांस लेने में तकलीफ़ के संकेतों पर नज़र रखें [1]। सांस लेने में दिक्कत, तेज़ सांस चलना, पसलियाँ धँसना या सांस में सीटी की आवाज़ होना — ये सब संकेत हैं कि तुरंत डॉक्टर से मिलना ज़रूरी है [1]।

अगर बच्चे की हालत बिगड़ती दिखे या डॉक्टर से मिलने के बाद भी सुधार न हो, तो तुरंत डॉक्टर से मिलें [3]।

q: मेरे 5 साल के बच्चे के शरीर पर लाल दाने हो गए हैं और खुजली है
text:
5 साल के बच्चे में बहुत खुजली वाले छोटे दाने स्केबीज़ (खुजली रोग) के कारण हो सकते हैं — यह छोटे कीड़े होते हैं जो त्वचा में घुसकर अंडे देते हैं, जिससे तेज़ खुजली और दाने होते हैं [2]। अक्सर उंगलियों के बीच उभरी हुई लकीरें दिखती हैं जिनके एक सिरे पर बिंदु होता है, और स्केबीज़ का इलाज आमतौर पर घर पर ही हो सकता है [4]।

इलाज क्रीम या मुँह से ली जाने वाली दवा से होता है [2]। इलाज शुरू करने के बाद बच्चा स्कूल जा सकता है, लेकिन पहले 24 घंटे दूसरों से नज़दीकी संपर्क से बचें [1]। इलाज कीड़ों को जल्दी मार देता है, पर खुजली कुछ हफ़्ते तक बनी रह सकती है [1]। दवा की मात्रा और तरीका डॉक्टर या दवा के पर्चे के अनुसार ही दें।

डॉक्टर से मिलें अगर फार्मेसी के इलाज के 2 से 4 हफ़्ते बाद भी खुजली बनी रहे, त्वचा में संक्रमण लगे या कोई और त्वचा रोग जैसे एक्ज़िमा हो [1]। खुजाने से त्वचा में संक्रमण हो सकता है [1]।

q: क्या एमएमआर वैक्सीन बच्चे के लिए सुरक्षित है
text:
हाँ, टीके काफी सुरक्षित हैं [6]। लगभग सभी वैक्सीन्स के थोड़े-बहुत दुष्प्रभाव हो सकते हैं, जो मामूली से गंभीर तक हो सकते हैं, पर ये सारे टीके काफी सुरक्षित हैं और मामूली उपचार से दुष्प्रभाव ठीक हो जाते हैं [6]। दुष्प्रभाव होना यह संकेत है कि वैक्सीन अपना असर दिखा रही है [6]।

एमएमआर वैक्सीन के बारे में: नियमित टीकाकरण कार्यक्रम में एमएमआरवी वैक्सीन की पहली खुराक एक साल की उम्र में दी जाती है [1]। भारत में टीकों की उम्र और खुराक राष्ट्रीय टीकाकरण कार्यक्रम के अनुसार तय होती है, इसलिए अपने बच्चे के टीकाकरण की तारीखें अपने डॉक्टर या स्वास्थ्य कार्यकर्ता से पूछ लें [3]। अगर बच्चे की कोई खुराक छूट गई हो, तो डॉक्टर से मिलकर बताएँ कि कौन-सा टीका कब लगवाना है [3]।

q: 3 saal ke bacche ko raat ko bahut khansi aati hai
text:
Raat ki khansi 3 saal ke bachche mein aam hai — khaas taur par asthma mein, jismein khansi raat ko ya subah jaldi hoti hai [5]. Agar bachche ko saans lene mein takleef, tez saans, ya seene mein jakadan bhi ho, to yeh asthma ke lakshan ho sakte hain [5].

Ghar par: bachche ko aaram karne dein aur khoob saara paani ya tarvish pilayein [4]. Khansi ya zukaam ke liye koi bhi dawa dene se pehle apne doctor ya pharmacist se poochein, kyunki kuch cough-cold dawaiyan bachchon ke liye theek nahi hoti [4]. Aspirin bilkul na dein [4].

Turant madad lein agar saans lene mein sakht takleef ho, hoth ya chehra neela ya safed dikhe, ya bachcha bahut sust ya so sa gaya lage [5][7].

q: mera 8 month ka baby bed se gir gaya aur ro raha hai
text:
Aapke 8 mahine ke baby ko bed se girne ke baad sar par chot lagi hai. SEUP ke mutabik sar par chot ke aam lakshan sir dard, chakkar, ulti aur neend aana hain [1].

Ghar par unhe aaram dein — 24 se 48 ghante tak sharirik aur mansik aaram, koi khel ya screen nahi [2]. Agar sir dard ho to paracetamol ya ibuprofen unki doctor ki batayi hui khurak mein de sakte hain [6]. Khane mein koi khaas badlav ki zarurat nahi, apni bhookh ke hisaab se khilate rahein [6]. Unhe sone dein, lekin zyada badi chot mein har 4 ghante jagakar check karna theek hai [6].

Turant madad lein agar sir dard badhta jaye ya kam na ho, baar-baar ulti ho, ve confused ya sust ho, behoshi ke kareeb hon, baat ya chalne mein dikkat ho, jhatke aayen, ya naak ya kaan se khoon ya saaf paani aaye [2][4].

q: 5 saal ke child ko body pe red rashes ho gaye hain
text:
5 saal ke bachche mein red rashes ke kai kaaran ho sakte hain, aur WHO ke mutabik sarna (scabies) mein bhi sharir par dane aur kharish hoti hai [1][4]. Sarna mein tez kharish hoti hai, khaas taur par raat mein, aur ungliyon, kalaiyon, baahon, pairon aur kamar ke aas-paas dane aur lakeerein dikhti hain [1]. Chhote bachchon mein yeh rash hathon ki hatheliyon, pairon ke talwon aur sar ki twacha par zyada gambhir ho sakta hai [1].

Agar aapko lagta hai ki yeh sarna hai, to bachche ko doctor dikhaiye — sarna ka ilaaj cream ya dawa se hota hai [4]. Sarna seedhe twacha ke sampark se phailti hai [4].

Kharish ya rash ke saath agar twacha par infection ke lakshan dikhein, to turant doctor se milein [1].

q: kya polio ki drop dena zaroori hai
text:
Polio ki drop dena zaroori hai. Ministry of Sanidad ke mutabiq polio (VPI) ka teeka bachpan ke niyamit vaccination calendar ka hissa hai, jo 2, 4 aur 11 mahine ki umar mein diya jata hai [3]. Jo bachche 2, 4 aur 11 mahine par ye teeke le chuke hain, unhe 6 saal ki umar par DTPa/VPI ka combined teeka diya jata hai [3].

Agar aapke bachche ki koi dose chhoot gayi hai, to jitni jaldi ho sake apne doctor se mil kar pending doses poori karwaiye — teeke bina der shuru karne chahiye [1]. Vaccination ke waqt apne doctor se ye bhi poochh lijiye ki aapke bachche ki umar ke hisaab se kaunse teeke baaki hain [1].

q: my baby has diarrhea after we came back from a trip
text:
Diarrhoea is usually a sign of an infection in the digestive tract, and it can be caused by many different bacteria, viruses and parasites, according to the WHO [6]. It is often picked up from contaminated food or water, or from person to person when hygiene is poor [6].

Give oral rehydration salts (ORS) — a mixture of clean water, salt and sugar — and keep offering nutrient-rich foods, including breast milk, during the episode [1]. Zinc supplements are also part of treatment: they shorten the episode by about 25% and reduce stool volume by about 30% [1]. Do not use homemade solutions or fizzy drinks to replace the losses, and do not give medicines for the diarrhoea or vomiting without asking your paediatrician, according to the SEUP [3].

See a health professional if the diarrhoea is persistent, if there is blood in the stool, or if there are signs of dehydration [1].

q: क्या टीका लगने के बाद बुखार आना सामान्य है?
text:
अगर बच्चा 3 महीने से छोटा है, तो बुखार होने पर उसी दिन डॉक्टर को दिखाना ज़रूरी है।

बड़े बच्चों में टीके के बाद हल्का बुखार आना सामान्य है और चिंता की बात नहीं है। डी.पी.टी. या डी.टी. का टीका लगने के कुछ घंटों बाद बच्चे को हल्का बुखार हो सकता है, और ये दुष्प्रभाव आम तौर पर 2-3 दिनों में अपने आप ठीक हो जाते हैं [5]। खसरे के टीके के 6-7 दिनों बाद भी हल्का बुखार और शरीर पर हल्के लाल दाने हो सकते हैं, जिनके लिए इलाज की ज़रूरत नहीं होती — ये लक्षण अपने आप ठीक हो जाते हैं [5]।

q: my child has been in the sun and now feels dizzy
text: Heat exhaustion does not usually need emergency medical help if you can cool down within 30 minutes, according to the NHS [4]. Dizziness is one of its symptoms, along with tiredness, headache, nausea, heavy sweating, pale clammy skin, cramps, thirst and irritability [4]. Someone showing signs of heat exhaustion needs to be cooled down and given fluids [4]. Move them out of the sun, into a cool place, and give them cold drinks [2][4]. Heatstroke is different and is a medical emergency: a very high temperature, hot skin without sweating, fast breathing and heartbeat, confusion, seizure or loss of consciousness — get immediate medical help for those [5]. While waiting, wrap them in a cool, wet sheet or sponge them with cold water [6].

q: my child has loose motions since morning what should I give
text:
Loose, watery stools are usually a short illness that goes away on its own, but the main risk is losing water and salts [4][2]. Give your child an oral rehydration solution to replace the fluids and electrolytes they have lost — you can buy these without a prescription [1][3]. Offer it in small sips often rather than a large amount at once. Keep breastfeeding or offering usual feeds. A 10–14 day course of zinc tablets can shorten how long diarrhoea lasts, according to the WHO [2].

Contact a health care provider right away if your child has a change in mental state such as irritability or lack of energy, diarrhoea lasting more than a day, any fever in an infant, frequent loose stools, vomiting often, severe belly or rectal pain, signs of dehydration such as thirst, dry mouth, urinating less than usual or no wet diapers for 3 hours or more, or stools that are black and tarry or contain blood or pus [6].

q: is MMR vaccine safe for my daughter
text: Yes, the MMR vaccine is safe. Like all medicines it can cause side effects, but not everyone gets them, and the common ones are usually mild and last only 2 to 3 days, according to the NHS [4]. These can include a raised, blotchy rash, feeling unwell and a high temperature around 7 to 11 days after the vaccination, or swollen glands around the cheeks, neck and jaw and aching joints around 2 to 3 weeks after it [4]. More serious side effects, such as a severe allergic reaction, are rare, and the person who vaccinates your child is trained to treat them immediately [4]. The MMR vaccine is not linked to autism: research has shown there is no link [4]. Protection starts within 2 weeks of the vaccine, and after 2 doses around 99% of people are protected against measles and rubella and around 88% against mumps [1]. In India, the ages for each dose follow India's national schedule.

text:
Around 6 months is the right time to start solid foods, and at first how much your baby eats matters less than getting them used to the idea [4]. They will still get most of their energy and nutrients from breast milk or first infant formula [4].

You can offer a wide variety of foods alongside milk from around 6 months, and this helps set your child up for healthier eating [4]. There is no right or wrong way to feed — spoon feeding, letting your baby feed themselves, or a mix of both all work [1]. What matters most is that your baby eats a wide variety of food and gets the nutrients they need [1].

Make sure your baby is sitting safely upright in a high chair with a securely fitted harness, and never leave them unattended on raised surfaces [5]. Introduce a cup from around 6 months and offer sips of water with meals [5].

q: my 5 year old has stomach pain and constipation
text:
Stomach ache is a common symptom in children and most causes are harmless and get better on their own, such as constipation, gas or a tummy bug, according to the SEUP [2]. Constipation often comes with a stomach ache and feeling bloated or sick [1].

For the constipation, the main thing is to offer more fluids, preferably water, and more fibre — wholegrain cereals and bread, fruit and vegetables. Don't replace fruit with juice, as juice has little fibre [3]. Keep to a regular routine and don't let your child hold in the urge to go to the toilet [3]. Most cases of childhood constipation (95%) are not caused by any illness, and it is not essential for a child to poo every day [3].

See your doctor rather than going to the emergency department, unless there is severe tummy pain, your child is very down and complaining a lot, there is blood in the poo, or they vomit many times and can't keep down solids or fluids [3].

q: my 3 year old has malaria fever or maybe teething, how can I tell
text: Malaria and teething are not told apart by the fever alone: the first symptoms of malaria may be mild and similar to many febrile illnesses, and hard to recognise as malaria, according to the WHO [1]. The most common early symptoms are fever, headache and chills [1]. Malaria is a life-threatening disease spread by mosquito bites, mostly in tropical countries, and it does not pass from person to person [1]. Children under 5 are at higher risk of severe infection [1]. If you are in or have travelled to an area where malaria is common, fever needs medical assessment — malaria is preventable and curable, and treatment can stop mild cases getting worse [1]. MedlinePlus adds that malaria can cause high fevers, shaking chills, flu-like symptoms and anaemia [2].

If your child is under 3 months old, a fever needs a doctor the same day.

For an older child, a high temperature is very common and usually settles within 1 to 4 days, according to the NHS [1]. A fever is 38C or more, and it is the body's natural response to fighting an infection [1][3]. Take their temperature with a digital thermometer under the arm, pressed against the side of the body [1]. Keep them hydrated with plenty of fluids, and do not undress them or sponge them down to cool them, or wrap them in too many clothes or blankets [3][7]. Do not give aspirin to a child under 16 [7]. See a doctor if the fever lasts 5 days or more, if they have a rash along with the fever, if they are not eating or not themselves, or if they are dehydrated, such as nappies that are not very wet, sunken eyes, and no tears when crying [7].

A severe cough with catarrh (a runny nose) can be the first phase of whooping cough, which starts like a cold with a runny nose, sneezing and a mild cough, according to the NHS [2]. In the first phase, which usually lasts 1 to 2 weeks, symptoms may include fever, runny nose, red watery eyes, and mild or occasional cough and sneezing [4].

If you think it could be whooping cough, see your doctor. Treatment depends on your age and how long you've had the infection, and if it is diagnosed within 3 weeks of the cough starting, antibiotics are given to help stop it spreading to others, though they may not reduce symptoms [6].

Whooping cough is less severe in older children, but the coughing can cause sore ribs, hernia, middle ear infections, or leaking pee when coughing [2].

q: my 3 year old has watery stool and weakness
text: Watery stools with weakness in a 3-year-old is diarrhoea, and the main risk is losing water and salts [3]. Give oral rehydration salts (ORS) — a mixture of clean water, salt and sugar — to replace the water and electrolytes lost in the stools [1]. Also give zinc supplements: they shorten the episode by about 25% and reduce stool volume by about 30% [1]. Keep giving nutrient-rich foods, including breast milk, during the episode [1]. Children with diarrhoea should be given oral rehydration solutions to replace lost fluids and electrolytes [6]. Contact a health professional for persistent diarrhoea, blood in the stool, or signs of dehydration [1]. For a child, warning signs include a change in mental state such as irritability or lack of energy, diarrhoea lasting more than a day, frequent loose stools, and signs of dehydration such as thirst, dry mouth, urinating less than usual or no wet diapers for 3 hours or more, and no tears when crying [2].

q: what can I give my 2 year old for diarrhoea
text: For a 2-year-old with diarrhoea, the main treatment is oral rehydration salts (ORS) — a mixture of clean water, salt and sugar that replaces the water and electrolytes lost in the stools, according to the WHO [1]. A baby who is passing urine less than usual may be dehydrated, and fewer wet nappies than usual is one of the signs to look for [3]. In infants, dehydration can also show as a dry mouth and tongue, crying without tears, no wet diapers for 3 hours or more, unusual sleepiness or irritability, or sunken eyes [1].

q: my baby fell from the bed and seems normal now
text:
A knock on the head from a fall is common, and most head injuries in children are mild and not dangerous [1][2]. If your baby seems normal now, the SEUP advises watching them closely for the first 24 hours after the blow, to catch any signs of something more serious [2].

During that time, keep them resting — no physical activity or screens for 24 to 48 hours, depending on how hard the knock was — and return to normal activities gradually [5].

Watch for: intense or worsening headache that does not improve with the usual medicine (paracetamol or ibuprofen), repeated vomiting, confusion or disorientation, and in very small babies, being irritable or hard to wake [5]. Also watch for behaviour changes, trouble speaking or walking, or blood or clear fluid from the nose or ears [5].

Go to the emergency department if any of those symptoms appear, if your baby is under three months old, or if the fall was from more than one metre [4].

q: my baby has been vomiting since yesterday and has fewer wet nappies
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Signs of dehydration: sunken eyes, little urine, dry mouth, persistent vomiting or heavy diarrhoea >24 h
text:
First, do what the warning above says.

Vomiting with fewer wet nappies can be a sign of dehydration, and babies lose fluid faster than older children, according to the SEUP [1]. Offer an oral rehydration solution — the ready-made kind, not homemade mixes or fizzy drinks — in small amounts often, and keep breastfeeding normally or more often if your baby wants it [1][7]. text:
Vomiting and loose stools together are usually caused by a stomach bug or food poisoning, according to the NHS [1]. Most babies with this get better on their own, but the main risk is dehydration [3].

Keep giving fluids. Offer an oral rehydration solution in small sips, often — this is the most important thing [3]. Keep breastfeeding normally, and more often if your baby wants it [5]. Do not water down formula — use it at its usual strength [6]. Do not give fruit juice or fizzy drinks, as they can make diarrhoea worse [6].

Vomiting usually stops in 1 or 2 days and diarrhoea within 5 to 7 days [6].

Get help if your baby is under 3 months and has vomited two or more feeds, is sleepy or floppy, has sunken eyes, cries without tears, or is passing little urine, according to the SEUP [2].

q: my son has fast breathing with cough

text: Fast breathing with a cough can be a sign of bronchiolitis, which often starts like a normal cold with cough and mucus, and after 2 to 4 days the child may breathe faster and find it harder to feed, according to the SEUP [3]. Keep them sleeping propped up semi-upright, and offer small, frequent feeds and fluids [6]. There is no medicine that cures bronchiolitis; most cases improve within about 2 weeks, though the cough can last longer [6]. Watch their breathing, how well they feed, their colour and their general state [6]. In children under 5 with cough or difficulty breathing, fast breathing or chest indrawing points to pneumonia, according to the WHO [7]. If the child is drowsy, very irritable or struggling to breathe, they need to be seen in the emergency department [2][5].

q: my 3 year old has fever 102, can I give Calpol
text:
102 °F = 38.9 °C.

Paracetamol can help if your child is distressed or uncomfortable because of a high temperature, according to the NHS [3]. It is a common painkiller for children that helps relieve pain and high temperature [4].

The main goal is your child's comfort — treat the discomfort, not the fever itself [2]. Make sure they drink plenty of fluids and are not over-wrapped, and keep the room at a neutral, ventilated temperature [2]. Paracetamol and ibuprofen can be given at the dose your paediatrician recommends, every 6–8 hours [2]. Do not routinely alternate the two every 3–4 hours unless your child is uncomfortable before the 6 hours are up [2]. Do not bathe them in cold water or put wet cloths on them — it is unpleasant and does not work [2]. It is normal for them not to want to eat; do not force it, but keep offering plenty of fluids [2].

q: can I give ORS to my 1 year old after diarrhea
text: Yes, you can give oral rehydration salts (ORS) to your 1-year-old after diarrhoea. The WHO lists rehydration with ORS as a key treatment for diarrhoea, and ORS is a mixture of clean water, salt and sugar that replaces the water and electrolytes lost in the stools [1]. Zinc supplements are also part of treatment: they reduce how long the diarrhoea lasts by 25% and cut stool volume by about 30% [1]. Keep giving nutrient-rich foods, including breast milk, during the episode [1]. Do not use homemade solutions or commercial soft drinks to replace the losses, and do not give medicines for diarrhoea or vomiting without asking your paediatrician, according to the SEUP [3]. The SEUP advises seeing a doctor if your child is very thirsty, cries without tears, urinates little or has sunken eyes, or is very irritable, drowsy or less responsive [3].

q: le ha salido un sarpullido rojo por las piernas y le pica
text:
Un sarpullido rojo que pica mucho en las piernas puede ser una urticaria: son ronchas o placas rojas y elevadas que pican, y en la infancia la mayoría están causadas por una infección, según la SEUP [3]. También puede tratarse de una reacción alérgica, que entre sus síntomas incluye picazón y sarpullidos [4], o de lesiones por picaduras de insectos, que pican intensamente y aparecen sobre todo en brazos y piernas [6].

Conviene evitar que se rasque, porque el rascado enrojece la piel y aumenta la hinchazón y el picor [1], y porque rascarse mucho puede infectar las lesiones [6]. Si sospechas que algún alimento o sustancia lo ha provocado, evita ese contacto [4].

Busca atención médica si aparece hinchazón de la cara, la lengua o los labios, o problemas para respirar [5].

q: mi hijo tiene conjuntivitis y se le pegan los ojos al despertarse
text: La conjuntivitis es una inflamación de la capa externa del ojo y del interior del párpado, y en la mayoría de los casos se cura sin tratamiento médico [2]. Para limpiar los párpados, hierve agua y déjala enfriar; luego pasa suavemente un algodón limpio por las pestañas para quitar las costras, usando un algodón distinto para cada ojo [5]. También puedes poner un paño frío sobre los ojos unos minutos para aliviarlos [5]. Si no estás seguro de que sea conjuntivitis, conviene descartar otras causas de ojo rojo [5]. Consulta a tu médico si tu hijo tiene menos de 30 días y los ojos rojos y pegajosos, si los síntomas no han mejorado en 7 días, o si hay dolor en los ojos, sensibilidad a la luz, cambios en la visión o los ojos muy rojos [1].

text:
Que se le marquen las costillas al respirar es un signo de dificultad respiratoria, y la SEUP indica que en ese caso hay que acudir a urgencias [1][5]. Aunque después se ponga a jugar, el esfuerzo de la respiración sigue ahí: la SEUP pide vigilar precisamente eso, que se marquen las costillas o se hunda el pecho, y consultar en urgencias cuando aparece dificultad para respirar [3].

Mientras llegan o van hacia allí, mantén al niño tranquilo y en una postura cómoda, semisentado, y ofrécele sorbos pequeños de líquido si lo acepta; si rechaza comer o beber de forma persistente, también es motivo de consulta [5]. No le des jarabes ni supositorios para la tos sin consultar con su pediatra [8].

Si además tiene mal color, está decaído, somnoliento o muy irritable, o respira cada vez más deprisa, son señales de que la dificultad respiratoria empeora [5][6].

text:
Si el bebé tiene menos de 3 meses, la fiebre necesita que lo vea un médico hoy mismo.

En un niño mayor, la fiebre y la rigidez de cuello juntas son motivo de atención médica inmediata: la meningitis puede agravarse muy rápido, y entre sus señales están la fiebre súbita y la rigidez en el cuello, según MedlinePlus [7]. Mientras llega la ayuda, mantén al niño acompañado y no le des nada por la boca si está somnoliento o no responde bien.

La meningitis bacteriana es rara, pero puede ser mortal, y el tratamiento temprano ayuda a prevenir problemas graves, incluida la muerte [7]. Los exámenes para diagnosticarla incluyen análisis de sangre, pruebas de imágenes y una punción espinal [7].

Mientras tanto, si tiene fiebre, asegúrate de que esté bien hidratado, en una habitación con temperatura neutra y sin sobreabrigarlo, según la SEUP [5]. No lo bañes en agua fría ni le pongas paños húmedos: resulta desagradable y no es eficaz [5].

q: mi bebe tiene 9 meses y todavia no tiene dientes
text:
La erupción de los dientes de leche empieza alrededor de los 6 meses, con los incisivos centrales inferiores, y sigue la secuencia habitual, según el Manual de Pediatría de la PUC Chile [6]. Que a los 9 meses todavía no le hayan salido no significa por sí solo que algo vaya mal: la edad de inicio varía de un bebé a otro.

Mientras tanto, puedes revisarle la boca con calma: mira los labios, la mucosa de las mejillas, las encías y la lengua, y aprovecha para empezar los cuidados de higiene bucal [6]. Si te preocupa que no le salga ningún diente, coméntalo en su próxima revisión con tu pediatra, que podrá examinarle la encía y los rebordes dentarios [6].

q: mi hija ha dejado de decir palabras que antes decía
text:
Perder palabras que antes decía es una señal para actuar pronto, no para esperar: si tu hija ha perdido habilidades que ya tenía, conviene hablar con su médico y pedir una evaluación del desarrollo, según los CDC [3].

No esperes a la próxima revisión. Cuéntale al médico qué palabras decía antes y cuándo dejó de usarlas, y pide una evaluación del desarrollo con herramientas estandarizadas [3]. La Academia Americana de Pediatría recomienda hacer cribados del desarrollo a los 9, 18 y 30 meses, y de autismo a los 18 y 24 meses, o en cualquier momento en que un padre o el médico tenga una preocupación [3].

Si tú o el médico seguís preocupados, pedid una derivación a un especialista que valore a tu hija más a fondo, y buscad el programa de atención temprana de tu zona para saber si puede recibir servicios de apoyo [3]. Cuanto antes empiecen los servicios de desarrollo —como terapia del habla—, mejor suele ser el resultado [5].

q: mi hijo de 15 años tiene dolor en el pecho despues de hacer deporte
text: El dolor de pecho tiene muchas causas y, en la mayoría de los casos, no se debe a un problema del corazón, según el NHS [2]. Un dolor que empieza después de hacer ejercicio o de una lesión en el pecho, que empeora al respirar hondo y mejora con el reposo, puede ser un esguince o una contractura muscular [2]. Si el dolor es agudo y continuo, aparece con preocupaciones o estrés y se acompaña de latidos rápidos, sudoración o mareos, puede deberse a ansiedad o a un ataque de pánico [2]; la SEUP también incluye la presión o el dolor en el pecho entre las señales de ansiedad [3]. No lo autodiagnostiques: si te preocupa, consulta a tu médico [2].

q: mi hija de 13 años tiene reglas muy abundantes
text:
Puede ser normal tener reglas abundantes, y a veces lo son más en distintas etapas, como al empezar con la regla [5]. Se consideran abundantes, según el NHS, si hay que cambiar la compresa o el tampón cada 1 o 2 horas, si se usan dos productos a la vez, si duran más de 7 días, si se expulsan coágulos mayores de unos 2,5 cm, si se mancha la ropa o la cama, si impiden las actividades diarias o si se siente mucho cansancio o falta de aire [1]. El tratamiento puede ayudar cuando afectan a la vida diaria [1].

Conviene ver al médico si las reglas abundantes afectan a su vida, si lleva tiempo así, si tiene dolor intenso, si sangra entre reglas o después de las relaciones, o si hay otros síntomas como dolor al orinar o al ir de vientre [5].

El desmayo o síncope es una pérdida de conocimiento brusca y corta: suele ocurrir cuando no llega suficiente sangre u oxígeno al cerebro, según la SEUP [1]. Antes de perder el conocimiento puede haber náuseas, visión borrosa, sudoración o zumbidos, y el niño se pone pálido y pierde la fuerza [2].

Si vuelve a sentirse mal, que se siente o se tumbe de inmediato, y que respire lenta y profundamente; si pierde el conocimiento, túmbala con las piernas elevadas y la cabeza de lado [5]. Cuando el malestar desaparezca, que se incorpore despacio: primero sentada y, tras unos minutos, de pie [5]. Tras un rato de reposo, los niños suelen recuperarse en un par de minutos [5].

Que beba más líquidos, sobre todo cuando hace ejercicio físico [4].

q: cuando se puede empezar con la fruta y la verdura
text:
La fruta y la verdura se pueden empezar a ofrecer en torno a los 6 meses, cuando la leche ya no cubre por sí sola las necesidades del bebé [2]. Según la AEP, no hay unas frutas mejores que otras para comenzar: se aconseja ir introduciendo toda la variedad disponible, en cualquiera de las comidas del día y variando la forma de presentarla (triturada, chafada, en trozos pequeños) [1].

Conviene ofrecer los alimentos de uno en uno, con intervalos de unos días, para ver cómo los tolera, y sin añadir sal ni azúcar [4]. Durante el primer año, evita las verduras de hoja verde con muchos nitratos, como acelga, espinaca o borraja; si las das, que sean menos del 20 % del plato, y hasta los 3 años no más de una ración diaria [1]. Mejor fruta entera que zumo: el zumo no aporta ventajas frente a la fruta y aumenta el riesgo de caries [1].

q: mi hija de 5 años tiene granitos rojos por la tripa que le pican mucho
text:
Los granitos rojos que pican mucho pueden ser varios tipos de sarpullido, y la mayoría se puede tratar en casa [3][5]. Si son manchas o bultitos elevados que pican, puede tratarse de urticaria, que suele tratarse en casa [5]. Si son puntitos pequeños y elevados con sensación de picor o escozor, puede ser sarpullido por calor [6].

Para calmar el picor, según el NHS, aplica algo frío, como un paño húmedo o una bolsa de hielo envuelta en un paño, durante un máximo de 20 minutos, y da golpecitos o palmaditas en el sarpullido en vez de rascarlo [6]. Para el sarpullido por calor, mantén la piel fresca: ropa de algodón holgada, ropa de cama ligera, baños o duchas frescas y beber abundante líquido; no uses geles ni cremas perfumadas [6].

Llama a tu número de emergencias si hay hinchazón alrededor de la boca o le cuesta respirar [5].

q: mi hijo es asmatico y se le hunden las costillas al respirar
banner: 🚨 Llama ahora al 112 o acude a urgencias. | Motivo: Dificultad para respirar grave (se marcan las costillas, respira muy rápido, pausas en la respiración, color azulado)
text: El hundimiento de las costillas al respirar (tiraje) es uno de los síntomas de una crisis asmática, según la SEUP [4]. En una crisis, administre de 2 a 4 pulsaciones de salbutamol, de una en una, con cámara espaciadora (y mascarilla facial en niños pequeños), y repita esa dosis a los 10-15 minutos [6]. Mantenga al niño en reposo, sin ejercicio, y lejos del humo del tabaco o de la contaminación [6]. Si toma tratamiento de mantenimiento, debe seguir con él durante la crisis [6]. Si la dificultad respiratoria empeora —respira cada vez más deprisa, se le marcan las costillas, mueve mucho el abdomen o se le hunde el pecho—, o si está muy agitado o somnoliento, hay que acudir a un servicio de urgencias, según la SEUP [3]. Si la crisis no cede tras el tratamiento en casa, acuda lo antes posible a un centro sanitario y lleve la cámara espaciadora [6].

text:
Paracetamol para 12 kg:
• Dosis: 180 mg cada 4–6 h (máx. 4 dosis/día).
  – Apiretal, gotas 100 mg/ml: 1.8 ml
  – jarabe 120 mg/5 ml: 7.5 ml
  – jarabe 125 mg/5 ml: 7.2 ml
  – jarabe 150 mg/5 ml (3 %): 6 ml

Comprueba siempre la concentración del envase. Si tiene menos de 3 meses, consulta antes de dar nada.

q: y si no le baja la fiebre le puedo dar dalsy
text:
Sí, se puede cambiar al ibuprofeno si el paracetamol no mejora el malestar. Según la SEUP, el paracetamol y el ibuprofeno se pueden dar a la dosis recomendada por su pediatra cada 6-8 horas, y ambos tienen una eficacia similar [1]. La AEPap concreta que, si damos un antitérmico y a las 3-4 horas la temperatura sigue alta y el malestar no mejora, es razonable intercambiarlos: si empezó con paracetamol y no mejora, la próxima vez se puede dar ibuprofeno [6].

Conviene saber que la fiebre puede persistir aunque se haya dado el antitérmico, sobre todo si era muy alta, y eso no significa que sea más grave [3]. El objetivo es el confort del niño, no bajar la fiebre a toda costa [1].

Consulte si el niño está decaído, poco reactivo o muy irritable, tiene dificultad para respirar, le aparecen manchas en la piel que no desaparecen al presionarlas, o no tolera sólidos ni líquidos [7].

banner: 🚨 Con estos síntomas hay que acudir a urgencias hoy, sin esperar. | Motivo: Signos de deshidratación: ojos hundidos, orina poco, boca seca, vómitos persistentes o diarrea abundante >24 h
text:
Lo primero, haz lo que dice el aviso de arriba.

Que un bebé pase hasta 24 horas sin hacer pis después de la primera micción puede ser normal, según la Junta de Andalucía [6]. Pasado ese tiempo, debe mojar los pañales con frecuencia, con orina clara e inodora, sobre todo si toma solo leche materna [6].

Si el bebé tiene mucha sed, llora sin lágrimas, orina poco o tiene los ojos hundidos, hay que consultar, según la SEUP [1]. Lo más importante es evitar la deshidratación ofreciendo soluciones de rehidratación oral ya preparadas, en pequeñas cantidades; no sirven las soluciones caseras ni los refrescos [1]. Si toma bien los líquidos, se le puede ofrecer su leche habitual (materna o de fórmula) y comida en pequeñas cantidades, sin forzarle [2].

q: mi hijo tiene diarrea pero quiere comer normal
text: La diarrea con gastroenteritis no suele ser grave y el niño puede seguir comiendo si tiene hambre, según MedlinePlus [1]. Lo más importante es evitar la deshidratación: ofrécele soluciones de rehidratación oral ya preparadas, en dosis pequeñas y tomas frecuentes, y la cantidad que te hayan indicado después de cada deposición líquida o vómito [3]. No uses soluciones caseras ni refrescos comerciales, y no le des medicamentos para la diarrea o los vómitos sin consultar con su pediatra [2]. Consulta pronto si la diarrea dura más de un día en un niño, si tiene fiebre alta, vómitos frecuentes, heces con sangre o pus, dolor abdominal intenso, o señales de deshidratación como boca seca, orinar menos o no mojar los pañales durante 3 horas o más [1].

q: mi hijo tiene manchas despues de tener fiebre, puede ser por la fiebre?
text:
Si el bebé tiene menos de 3 meses, la fiebre necesita que lo vea un médico ese mismo día [2].

En un niño mayor, las manchas rojas en la piel que no desaparecen al presionarla son un signo por el que hay que consultar en urgencias, según la SEUP [2]. La SEUP también pide vigilar en casa el estado general y el buen color del niño, y la aparición de petequias, esos puntos rojos que no se borran al apretar en sus laterales [1].

Si las manchas sí desaparecen al presionar, la SEUP las incluye entre los motivos para pedir consulta con el pediatra, no para urgencias [3].

¿Qué edad tiene? Con la edad afino la respuesta.

q: mi hijo tiene 2 años y 39 de fiebre desde ayer, le doy Apiretal?
text:
Con 39 de fiebre, lo importante es el malestar del niño, no el número: la fiebre es un mecanismo de defensa y no es sinónimo de gravedad, según la SEUP [3]. El objetivo del tratamiento es que el niño esté cómodo, no bajar la fiebre en sí misma [1].

El Apiretal (paracetamol) es uno de los antitérmicos más usados y se puede dar a la dosis que recomiende su pediatra, cada 6-8 horas [1]. La dosis depende del peso del niño; puedes calcularla con la calculadora de PediBot. No alternes paracetamol e ibuprofeno cada 3-4 horas salvo que el niño tenga malestar antes de las 6 horas [1].

Asegúrate de que beba abundantes líquidos, no lo fuerces a comer y no lo sobreabrigues ni lo bañes en agua fría [1]. Es normal que la fiebre dure entre 2 y 4 días, y que no baje del todo tras el antitérmico [4].

Consulta en urgencias si está decaído, poco reactivo o muy irritable, si le cuesta respirar, si no tolera líquidos ni sólidos, o si le salen manchas en la piel que no desaparecen al presionarlas [7].

q: mi bebe tiene muchos mocos y le cuesta dormir
text:
Los mocos y la dificultad para dormir encajan con un catarro de vías altas, una infección vírica de nariz y garganta muy frecuente en los primeros años, según la SEUP [3]. Es normal que los pequeños tengan entre 6 y 8 catarros al año [3].

En casa, ofrécele líquidos abundantes y hazle lavados nasales antes de las tomas y de dormir, preferiblemente con suero salino y nunca con agua del grifo [4]. Mantenlo lejos del humo y de lugares donde se fume [4]. No uses anticatarrales, mucolíticos, descongestivos ni jarabes para la tos, sobre todo si es menor de 6 años [4]. Si tiene fiebre por encima de 38 ºC y está incómodo, dale el antitérmico que suele recomendar su pediatra [4]. No le ofrezcas miel si es menor de un año [4].

La mucosidad puede durar hasta una semana; la tos, más de una semana [4].
